selection_rationale: cand-004 (Empirical Evaluation of RAG- and Tool-Poisoning Threats and Defenses) best balances novelty, falsifiability, venue relevance, and feasibility for CNSM’s Agentic AI Researcher track while directly addressing high-priority operational threat gaps; reviewer feedback is actionable and limited to preregistration-strengthening and ethical safeguards.
unresolved_uncertainties: U2: What is the end-to-end empirical efficacy of generate–verify–repair pipelines (LLM → validator → automated repair loop) in preventing operational outages at scale?
U3: How transferable are benchmark-derived failure modes (from emulated NetConfArena-like evaluations) to real operator environments with proprietary topologies, noisy telemetry, and human workflows?
U4: What operational thresholds and human-in-the-loop gating policies optimally balance safety and operator efficiency when allowing LLM-agent proposals to actuate network changes?
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Add an explicit ethical-safety plan: confine attacks to closed emulation, redact actionable payloads in public artifacts, and include safe-disclosure notes.
Preregister and justify a range of adversary models and threat strengths (document attack payloads internally; keep public descriptions high-level).
Define and preregister mitigation cost metrics (false-block rate, human-review workload proxies) and acceptable operational-impact thresholds.
Include ablation and scalability analyses for mitigations and instrument provenance/forensics signals to evaluate reproducibility and integration costs.
